drafts.title: Front seats offer longer adjustable thigh support and reliable memory restore for tall drivers
drafts.description: Tall drivers can extend the front seat thigh support and rely on the seat memory to restore their saved driving position consistently after others use the car.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Adjustable thigh-support extension range of at least 80 mm from the rear edge of the cushion; seat memory restores saved position within 10 mm linear deviation and 1° angular deviation of saved settings within 3 seconds on first recall in at least 95 of 100 consecutive trials.
assumptions: Ergonomic testing will validate 80 mm as a meaningful improvement for drivers ≥190 cm.
Electrical/mechanical actuators and control software can achieve the stated recall accuracy within 3 seconds.
Durability of memory function is validated over lifecycle testing (e.g., 10,000 cycles).
uncertainties: Exact baseline cushion dimensions vary by trim; final mechanical packaging may limit maximum extension.
Extreme occupant configurations (very small or very large) could affect perceived effectiveness.

drafts.title: Cup holders accept common bottle sizes and hold bottles securely
drafts.description: Customers can place typical bottles and travel mugs in the cup holders without tipping or excessive wobble during normal maneuvers.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Cup holder accommodates bottles up to 1000 ml and up to 90 mm base diameter; retains a vertical bottle without tipping during lateral acceleration of 0.3 g in at least 19 of 20 trials.
assumptions: Common 1 L bottles and travel mugs have base diameters ≤ 90 mm.
Interior packaging has space to enlarge cup-holder aperture without impacting other controls.
uncertainties: Some oversized travel mugs (>90 mm base) will still not fit.
Trim-specific center console layouts may require different cup-holder geometries.

drafts.title: Hands-free tailgate and flush door handles operate reliably in cold and freezing conditions
drafts.description: Customers can open the tailgate via the hands-free gesture and open the flush door handles in freezing or wet conditions without repeated attempts or manual thawing.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Hands-free tailgate opens on the first valid gesture within 3 seconds in at least 95 of 100 attempts after exposure to spray-and-freeze and at ambient −10°C; flush door handles unlock and open on the first attempt in at least 98 of 100 attempts under the same test conditions.
assumptions: Cold-weather validation tests (spray/freeze, salt exposure) will be used as the acceptance test protocol.
Access sensors and mechanisms can be designed or climate-protected to meet these reliability targets within the successor development window.
uncertainties: Extreme climates below −10°C or field conditions beyond test protocols may still cause occasional failures.
Aftermarket coatings or heavy contamination could degrade performance.

drafts.title: Ambient interior lighting provides many colors, brightness steps and user presets
drafts.description: Customers can personalize ambient lighting with a wide color palette, multiple brightness steps and saved presets to match mood and visibility needs.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: At least 64 distinct color choices, at least 10 discrete brightness levels, and at least 3 user-saveable lighting presets accessible from primary controls.
assumptions: LED-based lighting modules and the HMI will support 64 colors and multiple brightness steps.
Customers will use presets in real-world driving for quick recall.
uncertainties: Perceived difference between adjacent colors or brightness steps may vary by material and ambient light.
UX flow needs to ensure color/brightness selection is intuitive while driving.

drafts.title: Rear seating provides competitive legroom for adult passengers
drafts.description: Rear-seat occupants experience legroom comparable to main competitors so adults can sit comfortably for longer trips.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Rear knee clearance (measured from forward-most point of rear seat cushion to back of front seat) of at least 1000 mm when the front seat is set to the 95th-percentile driver position; production sample mean across 5 vehicles must meet or exceed this target.
assumptions: 1000 mm knee clearance is aligned with or slightly above typical executive-segment competitors and will meet customer expectations.
Front-seat adjustment range and packaging can be balanced to achieve this target without compromising crash or safety packaging.
uncertainties: Final competitor benchmarks may shift; if competitors increase legroom, target may need revision for future generations.
Trade-offs with other interior features (rear HVAC, center tunnel) may constrain achievable dimension.

drafts.title: Trunk includes a customer-accessible 12 V outlet capable of powering a cooler box
drafts.description: Customers can plug in and run a portable 12 V cooler from the trunk socket while driving or parked.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Dedicated 12 V socket in the trunk capable of supplying 12 V at up to 10 A continuously (120 W); verified by powering a 120 W cooler in the trunk for 30 minutes without fault.
assumptions: Electrical system can safely provide 10 A continuous to the trunk outlet without impacting other vehicle systems.
Fuse and thermal protection are included to meet vehicle safety requirements.
uncertainties: Some aftermarket coolers may draw spikes above continuous rating and require additional protection.
Location and sealing of outlet must ensure weather resistance for long-term reliability.
